list.item: Definition of Admiralty Islands as a strategic area with boundaries: 1°30′ and 3°10′ south latitude, 145°50′ and 148°10′ east longitude.
Designation of Australia as administering authority of the trust territory.

A clause or clauses giving Australia full legislative and administrative control in the trust territory subject only to the provisions of the Charter of the United Nations and the terms of the Trusteeship agreement. The clause or clauses should be so drawn as to make it clear that the United States possesses no responsibilities, rights, or powers with respect to the administration of the territory and its inhabitants.

The administering authority may establish, maintain, and control such bases, facilities, and forces, and take such measures for their security, as it may deem necessary or desirable in the trust territory.

Nothing in this trusteeship agreement shall preclude the administering authority from maintaining existing agreements and entering into such additional agreements as it may deem necessary or desirable with another member of the United Nations with respect to sharing rights of occupation and operation, and responsibility for the establishment, maintenance and control of existing or additional military bases and facilities in the trust territory [i.e., the Admiralty Islands strategic area], provided, however, that no such agreements shall preclude the offer of such bases and facilities to the Security Council of the United Nations on its call.

The amendment, alteration, or termination of this Trusteeship agreement shall be only by unanimous agreement of the signatories [i.e. the States directly concerned], subject to the approval of the Security Council.
